question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}9 & 2 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix $A$ above has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=10.$ Find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that $D={P}^{T}\,AP.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that a matrix $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable if there exists an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that

$$
A=PD{P}^{T},
$$

where $D$ is a diagonal matrix. Equivalently,

$$
D={P}^{T}AP.
$$

Moreover, a matrix $A$ is orthogonally diagonalizable if and only if it is symmetric.

Note that $A$ is symmetric. Therefore, it is orthogonally diagonalizable. Let's now go through the process.

**Step 1.**  Notice that we already have the eigenvalues of $A:$

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=5\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{2}=10$

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$ 

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 2 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-5I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{1}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{1}‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-10I & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 2 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-10I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{2}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{2}‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}].
$$

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the orthogonal matrix $P$ in the usual way, and this gives us the following:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 10\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$
